digest.greeting: Good morning, Jean. Monday, September 28 has five calendar commitments, eight carried-over actions, and five urgent items. The day’s priorities are setting an Amazon Connect go/no-go posture at the 10:30 AM standup, resolving the Attorney Review launch and coverage plan, using the afternoon portfolio sequence to close ownership decisions, and reviewing the CFO-backed Proactive Payday Notification intake. Amazon Connect remains the clearest delivery risk because Salesforce had not identified a root cause by Friday. Dashboard completion state is about a week old, so carry-over may lag newer check-offs.

items.label: Set Amazon Connect coverage and the revised Denver path
items.detail: Salesforce still had no root cause or resolution Friday, despite escalation to the account executive. Use the 10:30 AM standup to set the go/no-go posture for Denver, confirm decision coverage, and close the remaining user, skill, testing, training, and communications prerequisites.

items.label: Choose the Attorney Review launch and coverage plan
items.detail: More than 23 appointments are booked for the October 17 Salt Lake City opening, while the Service Cloud package needs to be testable before October 15. Confirm attorney coverage and whether rollout remains October 17 or moves to October 19.

items.label: Record and communicate the RFE MHE hold
items.detail: The project remains paused while Legal guidance and historical data are reviewed, and the September 30 target no longer applies. Document the review owners, the trigger for resuming planning, and the effect on scope and timing.

items.label: Confirm all five team self-reviews with HR
items.detail: Jean told HR that the team had completed the self-reviews, but a later HR message still listed Laura and Mar. Confirm all five submissions are recorded as complete before closing the task.

items.label: Set the CM-CoE backlog and Sprint 19 path
items.detail: This has remained unresolved since September 14. Confirm owners and Sprint placement for the Phase 1 and Phase 2 requests, and set a follow-up date for the Timetrack feedback so the queue does not remain open-ended.

items.label: Connect with Amy on Incident Response communications
items.detail: Confirm the Bucket 6 notification trigger, communication owner, and remaining Incident Response Guide inputs with Amy, who is leading internal communications and PR.

items.label: Share the new legal-guidance protocol with the remaining PMs
items.detail: Explain when to include Leo, Raquel, or Cristian and ask teams to distinguish mandatory legal requirements from recommendations.

items.label: Clarify the held Quality-routing deadline
items.detail: Send the interim status, revised decision point, and communication owner while the work waits for the new Phase 1 matter-plan structure.

items.label: 8:00 AM - Approve timecards and prepare the week
items.detail: Clear approvals and turn Friday’s delegated readouts into today’s decision list. The open 9:00–10:30 AM window is the best early focus block.

items.label: 10:30 AM - Amazon Connect daily standup
items.detail: Bring the unresolved Salesforce escalation, completed transfer testing, and the remaining user-skill assignment work. Leave with a Denver go/no-go posture and named owners.

items.label: Noon–1:30 PM - Protected work block
items.detail: Use the 90-minute block for Amazon Connect and Attorney Review follow-through before the afternoon meetings.

items.label: 2:00 PM - BD Portfolio Review
items.detail: Review active-project risks, new intake, and ownership decisions. Use the half hour before the 1:1s to settle the new-client scoping path and next commitments.

items.label: 3:00–4:00 PM - Back-to-back 1:1s with Maria and Rahul
items.detail: Use Maria’s discussion for portfolio roadblocks and next steps, then carry the decisions directly into the Rahul EPMO touchpoint.

items.label: Review the Proactive Payday Notification intake
items.detail: Hassan submitted the request as urgent and said it comes from the CFO. Confirm its priority, scope, and next owner today so the new intake does not sit untriaged.

items.label: Plan the newly launched downward reviews
items.detail: Both the W-2/EOR and freelancer year-end feedback cycles opened over the weekend. Check the assigned reviews, deadlines, and preparation needed, then reserve writing time.

items.label: Eugenia Barragán is out through October 1
items.detail: Route time-sensitive CoE and portfolio decisions around her absence.

items.label: 10:30 AM - Jhara 1:1 conflicts with the Amazon Connect standup
items.detail: Choose coverage or move one meeting so neither Jhara’s portfolio review nor the deployment decision is lost.

items.label: 11:00 AM - EPMO weekly slides focus block
items.detail: Protect the 30 minutes immediately after the morning conflict to keep the weekly update moving.

items.label: 2:00 PM - CM-CoE review overlaps the EPMO leadership catch-up
items.detail: The meetings begin together, and the leadership catch-up runs an hour. Assign coverage and define the decisions each readout must capture.

items.label: 3:30–4:30 PM - Nicolas 1:1 and CSC portfolio review
items.detail: Use the final hour for portfolio ownership and the initial CSC review, with a clean handoff between the two meetings.
